query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using vapor-coated W powders sintered via spark-plasma sintering can produce a uniform W-Cu material with improved thermal transport properties compared to conventional casting methods.
generation.material_initial_state: W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: Vapor-coating W powders and sintering via spark-plasma sintering
generation.conditions: High-temperature and high-pressure conditions during spark-plasma sintering
generation.structural_mediator: Uniform distribution of W particles in the Cu matrix
generation.mechanism: Enhanced contact between W and Cu constituents due to vapor-coating, leading to improved thermal transport properties
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity and reduced void formation compared to conventional casting methods
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the optimal vapor-coating and sintering parameters for achieving uniform W-Cu structures

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of thermal transport properties and microstructure of W-Cu materials fabricated via vapor-coated W powders sintered via spark-plasma sintering and conventional casting methods
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity of the vapor-coated W powders sintered via spark-plasma sintering is not significantly higher than that of the conventional casting method, the hypothesis is falsified.
